title: Ghost sightings expected at Milton Keynes Safari Park with Madagas-scare
excerpt: Visitors to Woburn Safari Park this Halloween are almost guaranteed a Ghost sighting...
content:

Visitors to Woburn Safari Park this Halloween are almost guaranteed a Ghost sighting...

The park will host its ‘Madagas-scare’ charity weekend on Saturday 31 October and Sunday 1 November in aid of Impact Madagascar.  

The Ghost in question is a four-year-old black-and-white ruffed lemur (called Ghost), and his name is fitting for the time of the year.

The word ‘lemur’ comes from the lemures, the restless spirits of the dead in Roman mythology.

The 18thcentury naturalist Carl Linnaeus chose it because of the animals’ nocturnal habits, reflective eyes and quiet movement through the trees. 

In some Malagasy communities, certain lemurs are also believed to embody the spirits of ancestors. These animals are treated with respect, with traditional taboos known as “fady” helping protect them from harm.

But behind the spooky name is a serious story: black-and-white ruffed lemurs are classed as Critically Endangered. 

"Halloween is a great opportunity to introduce visitors to our lemurs," said James Fryer, Deputy Team Leader, Animal Encounters at Woburn Safari Park, "But the truly scary story is how threatened they are in the wild, with lemurs as a group among the most at-risk mammals on the planet.

"We hope people come for the Halloween connection and leave knowing more about why these animals need protecting, and that the money raised will support Impact Madagascar's vital conservation work."

Keepers will be spending Halloween weekend raising money for Impact Madagascar, an organisation that helps protect endangered wild lemur species.

Visitors can meet the team, learn more about the species, book Mini VIP experiences and take part in games. There’s also the chance to win a VIP Close Up Encounter, listen to the spooky keeper talks and enjoy a trip on the ghost train.

Visitors hoping for a Ghost sighting can see him and the park’s other lemurs in the Land of the Lemurs. Book your tickets for some Halloween Half Term fun: https://www.woburnsafari.co.uk/news-and-events/events/october-half-term/
